verdict.rationale: LiteLLM's proxy documents an MCP Gateway. Users can register MCP servers through the UI ("Add New MCP Server"), expose all their tools behind one fixed endpoint with access controlled per key and team, and call those tools over REST. Missing for 10: documentation of models automatically invoking registered MCP tools inside completion requests, transport and auth configuration details, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: LiteLLM Proxy provides an MCP Gateway that allows you to use a fixed endpoint for all MCP tools and control MCP access by Key, Team.
On the LiteLLM UI, Navigate to "MCP Servers" and click "Add New MCP Server".
